prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1033; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a side impact collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver's side by a vehicle that entered on a red signal. Claimant reports left knee pain and limited mobility after the impact. Police report requested. Photos of both vehicles received from the insured.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and says they are handling the matter directly. Claimant describes striking the left knee on the door frame during impact and has ongoing pain when bending or bearing weight. Claimant states they visited an urgent care clinic the same day. Requested copies of visit records and imaging, if any, with signed authorization.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report. Officer noted the other driver admitted to not stopping for the red light. Witness statement from a pedestrian at the corner supports the account that the at-fault vehicle entered the intersection late. Liability appears clear in favor of our insured, pending final review of the scene diagram.

Entry 4: Received medical documentation from the urgent care clinic. Diagnosis listed as a contusion and sprain of the left knee. Recommended follow-up with an orthopedic provider if symptoms persist beyond two weeks. Claimant has not yet scheduled that follow-up. Sent a letter explaining the claim process and the right to request an independent medical review.

Entry 5: Followed up with the claimant. Claimant reports the knee is improving with rest and over-the-counter pain relief but still feels unstable on stairs. Discussed that the claim file will remain open until treatment is complete and a final medical report is received. Scheduled a reminder to recheck status in thirty days and to confirm the orthopedic referral was followed through.
